body.statement: If \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\), then for every \(\varepsilon\ge0\), \(\Pi_P\) maps \(\mathcal C_P^{\varepsilon}\) into \(\mathcal C_P\) and \(\|v-\Pi_P(v)\|_\infty\le\varepsilon\). The constant one is sharp. For every component-respecting mesh, the uniform-norm Hausdorff distance satisfies \(d_H(\mathcal C_{P,h},\mathcal C_P)=e_h\); hence each signed support value over \(\mathcal C_{P,h}\) differs from its full-class counterpart by at most \(\|\nu_P\|_{\mathrm{TV}}e_h\).
body.justification: Exact clipping replaces uncheckable strict-feasibility and active-set assumptions by a global deterministic stability certificate.
body.gap: Generic LP perturbation theory begins from a finite program and does not give this constant-one continuum feasibility retraction.
body.consumer: The certificate makes support gridding auditable and allows conservative endpoint computation even at equality constraints.
body.proof_tex:
Assume \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\).  Obstacle compatibility gives \(\ell_P\leq r_P\), and both obstacles are \(L\)-Lipschitz.  If \(v\in\mathcal C_P^{\varepsilon}\), the same propagation used for the exact obstacle characterization, now with the relaxed cone, gives
\[
\ell_P(x)-\varepsilon\leq v(x)\leq r_P(x)+\varepsilon
\qquad(x\in X_0).
\]
Indeed, the unrelaxed level constraints handle the constant obstacle pieces and each relaxed support inequality contributes at most \(\varepsilon\).  Pointwise projection onto the interval \([\ell_P(x),r_P(x)]\) is exactly \(\Pi_P(v)(x)\); hence
\[
|v(x)-\Pi_P(v)(x)|\leq\varepsilon.
\]
The maximum or minimum of two real-valued \(L\)-Lipschitz functions is again \(L\)-Lipschitz, as follows from
\[
|\max\{a,b\}-\max\{c,d\}|\leq\max\{|a-c|,|b-d|\},
\]
and the analogous inequality for minima.  Therefore \(\Pi_P(v)\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz and lies between the exact obstacles.  Obstacle compatibility implies
\[
\Pi_P(v)\in\mathcal C_P,
\qquad
\|v-\Pi_P(v)\|_\infty\leq\varepsilon.
\]
The factor one cannot be reduced: take a singleton \(X_0\), one support point with nonzero \(z\), \(g=0\), \(K=0\), and \(M\geq\varepsilon\).  Then \(\mathcal C_P=\{0\}\), while the relaxed class contains the constant \(v=\varepsilon\), whose distance to \(\mathcal C_P\) is exactly \(\varepsilon\).

For the mesh class, omission of constraints implies
\[
\ell_{P,h}\leq\ell_P\leq r_P\leq r_{P,h}.
\]
Any fixed member of \(\mathcal C_P\) lies between \(\ell_{P,h}\) and \(r_{P,h}\), so the mesh obstacles are ordered and both \(\ell_{P,h}\) and \(r_{P,h}\) belong to \(\mathcal C_{P,h}\).  Also \(\mathcal C_P\subseteq\mathcal C_{P,h}\).  For any \(v\in\mathcal C_{P,h}\), exact clipping gives a member of \(\mathcal C_P\), and pointwise
\[
|v-\Pi_P(v)|
\leq\max\{\ell_P-\ell_{P,h},r_{P,h}-r_P\}
\leq e_h.
\]
Thus the Hausdorff distance is at most \(e_h\).  Conversely, for every \(u\in\mathcal C_P\),
\[
\|u-\ell_{P,h}\|_\infty
\geq\|\ell_P-\ell_{P,h}\|_\infty,
\qquad
\|u-r_{P,h}\|_\infty
\geq\|r_{P,h}-r_P\|_\infty,
\]
because \(u\geq\ell_P\) and \(u\leq r_P\).  The two mesh obstacles therefore attain the two lower bounds, proving
\[
d_H(\mathcal C_{P,h},\mathcal C_P)=e_h.
\]
Finally, if two nonempty compact classes are within Hausdorff distance \(e_h\), continuity of \(J_P\) and \(\|\nu_P\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\leq1\) give, for either the maximum or minimum support value,
\[
|V_h-V_P|\leq\|\nu_P\|_{\mathrm{TV}}e_h.
\]
